title: bug: a sibling session's landing marks the shared task baseline landed=1 under a live rework session, so that session's crash is never recovered
description:
DEFECT (governor-filed 2026-09-18, second occurrence). The per-task baseline `<gitdir>/moe/baseline/<taskId>.tsv` is shared by every session that holds the task. Every landing rewrites it with `landed=1`: moe-agent.ps1:3816 after a committed landing, :3647 and :3747 for nothing/refused. It does this even when the baseline was last taken by ANOTHER session that is still open and has not landed. The recovery gate (Invoke-MoeRecoveryCheck, ps1:3934-3970) skips recovery whenever `landed=1`. So if that other session later dies, the next pre-flight never lands its bytes as a recovered checkpoint. It then re-takes the baseline over the dirty tree instead, and ps1:4005-4007 files any dirty path that is not ASSERTED/touched/unattributed/inferred as "inter-session dirt presumed foreign".

TRIGGER: every qa_reject followed by an immediate rework claim. The QA wrapper lands its exit checkpoint a few minutes AFTER the worker's pre-flight has taken the baseline, so every rework session runs under a baseline that says landed=1.

EVIDENCE, task-49ec8755:
- 09-17 17:41:53Z: qa-17c2d0c8 rejects (reopen #2). worker-3b5de06f claims the rework in the same second; its pre-flight writes the baseline (landed=0) and its live marker.
- 17:45:20Z: QA's exit landing commits checkpoint 1549402 and rewrites the baseline with landed=1 (file mtime 17:45:20Z).
- 18:57-18:59Z: the worker completes steps 5-6 (both launchers, both harnesses, both parity checks, docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and starts step 7. It then loses its seat to the 20:00:44Z daemon restart with no landing and no rescue ref (WORKER_TIMEOUT 21:05:44Z).
- 09-18 05:08:03Z: worker-d0c3b06e's pre-flight reads landed=1. It skips recovery (no MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED, no commit) and re-takes the baseline; header is now `at=2026-09-18T05:08:03Z head=a5fe0f9 landed=0`.
- The bytes survived only because all 7 paths were completed-step modifiedFiles (ASSERTED).
FIRST OCCURRENCE: task-9e851 on 09-14. QA's pre-flight at 19:26:33Z re-took the baseline over 4 dirty rework files without recovering (governor #governors 19:31Z; qa-f0f9ea9e suspected landed=1).

WHAT STRANDS: a path the dead session changed that is not ASSERTED and has no TOOL witness. Example: the edits of an IN_PROGRESS step on a codex/grok/gemini seat, which have no tool hook. That path lands in the new baseline's B set, becomes PREEXISTING, and no session ever commits it. It is not deleted, but it stays unlanded until some later edit touches the same file. The clean split of the dead session's bytes into their own checkpoint is lost too.

DIRECTION (the architect decides): scope `landed` to the session that took the baseline. For example, the header could record the pre-flight session id, and a landing would set landed=1 only when that id is its own; otherwise it prunes B and keeps landed=0. Another option is to key the flag to the live-marker owner. A session's own completed landing must still suppress replay on idle polls. The sh twin has the same flag (baseline_landed / baseline_write … 1 / baseline_mark_landed); verify it mirrors the ps1 path.
definitionOfDone: Both postflight harnesses (sh and ps1) gain a case that fails on the current launchers. Session A pre-flights task T and edits a planned path that is not asserted. Session B, another seat on T, lands a checkpoint. A then dies without landing. Session C's pre-flight on T must land MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED containing A's edit.

A landing never sets landed=1 on a baseline whose latest pre-flight belongs to a different, still-open session. A session's own completed landing still sets it, and the existing no-replay-on-idle-poll cases stay green.
The ps1 and sh twins behave identically, and parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 both pass.
The stale-marker recovery path (the 2026-08-28 lost-code fix) is unchanged: a dead owner's un-landed baseline is still recovered.
taskRails: Wrapper-only change: scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-agent.sh plus their harnesses; keep both twins in exact parity.
Never weaken recovery of a dead owner's un-landed bytes; when unsure, recover (a spurious checkpoint is recoverable, a stranded edit is not).

implementationPlan.description:
Phases 1+4: the ps1 twin of the fix. The rule scopes `landed` to the session whose pre-flight took the baseline. This is a wrapper-only change and the daemon stays untouched.

BEFORE ANY EDIT: save the CURRENT launchers for the red proofs in steps 3-5. Write `git show HEAD:scripts/moe-agent.ps1` and `git show HEAD:scripts/moe-agent.sh` into a uniquely named scratch dir outside the repo, never a fixed name (mem:gotcha-duplicate-seat-wrapper-resume-clone). Put that HEAD sha in the step note.

Edit scripts/moe-agent.ps1 with the Edit tool so the file keeps LF and its UTF-8 BOM. Serena rewrites the whole file as CRLF (mem:gotcha-serena-edit-rewrites-crlf-on-windows). The symbols below were verified while planning; find them by name, not by line number.
(a) The header-format comment above Read-MoeBaseline. The header becomes `#moe-baseline v1 task=<id> at=<iso> head=<sha> landed=<0|1> session=<sid>`. `session` is the pre-flight's $moeSid, `<workerId>@<pre-flight UTC second>`, the same id as the Moe-Session trailer. It names the session whose pre-flight took this baseline. Only three writers may put landed=1: that session's own landing, a recovery landing, or a landing that found no baseline. A header with no session= (written by an older twin) belongs to nobody.
(b) Read-MoeBaseline: parse ` session=(\S+)` from the header line into a new `Session` key, '' when absent. Every other key stays unchanged.
(c) Write-MoeBaseline: add a trailing `[string]$Session = ''` parameter. The header becomes `... landed=$Landed session=$Session`. Always write the token, with an empty value when the session is unknown, exactly as the sh twin does.
(d) New `Get-MoeBaselineLandedFlag($Bl, [string]$Sid, [bool]$Recovered)` beside Set-MoeBaselineLanded. It returns 1 in three cases: $Bl is $null (a landing that found no baseline creates one, as today); $Recovered; or $Bl.Session is non-empty and -ceq $Sid. Otherwise it returns the header's own flag, [int]$Bl.Landed. The recovery case is load-bearing. A recovery runs only when the gate found no live owner, and the idle paths recover with a FRESH sid on every poll. Without that case, every poll would replay the same recovery. Give the helper a 3-4 line comment with the why: on 2026-09-17 (task-49ec8755), QA's exit landing rewrote a live rework session's baseline to landed=1, and that session's crash was never recovered. Name the twin, baseline_landed_flag.
(e) Invoke-MoeLanding: right after `$bl = Read-MoeBaseline $baselinePath`, compute two values ONCE: `$landedFlag = Get-MoeBaselineLandedFlag $bl $Sid $recovered` and `$blSession = if ($bl) { $bl.Session } else { $Sid }`. Replace the literal landed 1 with `$landedFlag $blSession` at all three baseline writes: the no-candidates nothing/refused return, the unchanged-tree nothing return, and the committed prune. A landing never changes the header's session. The B prune and the U replacement stay exactly as they are.
(f) Set-MoeBaselineLanded gains `[string]$Sid`. It writes `(Get-MoeBaselineLandedFlag $bl $Sid $false)` together with `$bl.Session`. Its one caller is the deliberate no-landing branch of the post-flight mode selection; that caller passes $moeSid. Update the comment: a sibling's deliberate exit must not mark another session's baseline landed.
(g) Invoke-MoePreflightBaseline: its Write-MoeBaseline call passes `0 $Sid`.
(h) Invoke-MoeRecoveryCheck: the gate logic stays UNCHANGED (DoD 4). Only refresh its landed=1 comment to say who may set the flag now.
Afterwards, grep the file: no Write-MoeBaseline call may still pass a literal landed 1.

error handling: the new parse sits inside Read-MoeBaseline's existing try/catch, which returns $null on any read failure. Write-MoeBaseline keeps its warn-and-return-$false contract, and a landing ignores that result as it does today. Nothing new can throw into a landing or a pre-flight.

Hot reload: repo-launched ps1 wrappers restart onto this file at their next loop boundary. Make the whole change in one coherent pass; the new parameters default to the old shape until the call sites switch. Then run `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile(<abs path>, [ref]$null, [ref]$e)` under BOTH powershell.exe and pwsh. It must report 0 errors.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 4: the sh twin. It applies the same rule and writes the same header bytes, in scripts/moe-agent.sh. The file is LF with no BOM; use the Edit tool.
(a) The header comment above baseline_path gets the same format and ownership text as the ps1 twin, naming the twin functions.
(b) baseline_write gains $6 = session. The header printf becomes `'#moe-baseline v1 task=%s at=%s head=%s landed=%s session=%s\n'`, with "${6:-}" as the last argument.
(c) New helper `baseline_session TASKID` prints the header's session= value, '' when the token or the file is absent (for example `head -n1 | sed -n 's/.* session=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p'`). New helper `baseline_landed_flag TASKID RECOVERED(true|false)` prints 1 when no baseline file exists, when RECOVERED=true, or when the header session is non-empty and equals $MOE_SID. Otherwise it prints 1 if `baseline_landed` holds, else 0. Both helpers ALWAYS return 0: the wrapper runs under `set -e`, and a non-zero status inside `x="$(...)"` aborts the whole wrapper. Both only print and set no globals, so calling them via $(...) is safe (mem:gotcha-bash-state-fn-subshell-swallows-globals).
(d) run_landing: capture `local bl_flag bl_session` where it calls baseline_read. That is the same point where ps1 reads $bl. When no baseline file exists, bl_session is MOE_SID. The three baseline_after_landing calls (committed, nothing, refused) pass "$bl_flag" "$bl_session" instead of the literal 1.
(e) baseline_after_landing gains $6 = session and passes it on to baseline_write.
(f) baseline_mark_landed: first compute the flag (`baseline_landed_flag "$1" false`) and the session (`baseline_session "$1"`) into locals, BEFORE the file is rewritten. Then call baseline_write with them. MOE_SID is the iteration's pre-flight id, set at the top of the loop.
(g) preflight_landing: the step-4 baseline write passes `0 "$MOE_SID"`.
(h) preflight_landing step 3, the recovery gate, stays UNCHANGED.

error handling: the helpers degrade to the old behaviour. A missing file gives flag 1 and the current session, as a no-baseline landing does today. An unreadable header gives an empty session, which is never 'own', so the header's flag is kept. baseline_write keeps its return-1-on-failure contract, and its callers keep their `|| true`.

Checks: run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`. Count CRLF before and after the edit; it must stay 0. Compare the header both twins print for the same inputs. Token order and spelling must be byte-identical, because a WSL sh seat and a Windows ps1 seat read each other's baselines in the same checkout.

Then `echo again > DIR/impl.txt` and do run 2, identical to run 1. Run 2 must NOT print MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED. There must still be exactly one task-blocked commit, and `git status --porcelain` must show ` M impl.txt`. Failure message: '(d) an idle poll replayed the recovery the previous poll already landed'. Only THEN assert that the saved run-1 header has ` landed=1` and still the worker-dead session, because a recovery never takes over the header.

implementationPlan.description:
Phase 5: regression, parity and the mutation proof. This step makes no edits. Run everything sequentially on a quiet box. Keep logs and RC files in a unique scratch dir: `( ... ) > log; echo RC=$? > rc`.
1. From Git Bash: `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`. It takes about 36-42 min; use 400 instead of 180 while a vitest fan-out runs on the box. It must PASS and print 'commit-scope scenarios run: 29'.
2. postflight.ps1 under powershell.exe AND under pwsh, both launched from PowerShell. Each must report 29.
3. `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` and the ps1 twin must both PASS. No new MOE_* code was added, so the code-family diff must stay empty.
4. `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts`. That test executes the real platform wrapper end to end, so it shows single-session delivery is unchanged.
5. Parsers: `bash -n` on the sh twin, and 0 errors from the PS parser on the ps1 twin under both engines.

Existing cases pin behaviour this change must NOT move, and they must stay green:
- M: recovery before launch plus the BLOCKED hold. ps1 M also asserts that run 1's own landing wrote landed=1.
- M2 (a)-(e): M2-c is the 2026-08-28 stale-marker recovery (DoD 4). They still use legacy session-less headers, so they double as back-compat proof.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
CHOSEN: record the pre-flight's session id in the baseline header as `session=<sid>`, the same `<workerId>@<pre-flight second>` id as the Moe-Session trailer. A landing writes landed=1 only when that id is its own, or when it is a recovery, or when no baseline existed before it. Every other landing still prunes B and replaces U as today, but writes back the header's OWN flag and session. The recovery gate is untouched.

REJECTED: key the flag to the live-marker owner. In the real trigger, the rework session's pre-flight leaves QA's LIVE marker in place, because a pre-flight never overwrites a live peer's marker. At QA's exit landing the marker is therefore still QA's own, and that rule would still write landed=1. Sub-case (a) is built so that design fails.

REJECTED: probe at landing time whether the header's session is still open. A landing cannot know whether that session will die later, and keeping the owner's flag is right either way. An owner that already landed left landed=1, which is kept. A crashed owner's landed=0 is exactly what must survive.

REJECTED: set landed=1 only for the own session. The idle paths (BLOCKED hold, resume cap) recover with a fresh sid on every poll, so every poll would replay the same recovery. Sub-case (d) pins the recovery exception.

REJECTED: put the pre-flight's process identity (pid, start token) in the header and probe it at the recovery gate. A wrapper process outlives its session, because it loops on to the next task. That would suppress recovery of a rescued or refused session's baseline whose wrapper has moved on.

REJECTED: a new log line or code for 'kept another session's flag'. The header's session= and landed= already tell that story, and a new code would widen the parity-check surface past the wrapper-only rail.

SEQUENCING: dependsOn now includes task-8fc35d31, which is WORKING on the same wrapper and harness files. Its red frozen arms and WIP hunks would otherwise ride into this task's whole-file landings, and the reverse would happen too (mem:gotcha-shared-file-hunks-land-under-first-committer). The fix lands before its tests, with red proofs taken on scratch trees, so the shared harness is never red for a peer's regression run.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Every baseline writer: ps1 Write-MoeBaseline is called from Set-MoeBaselineLanded, from Invoke-MoeLanding (no-candidates nothing/refused, unchanged-tree nothing, committed prune) and from Invoke-MoePreflightBaseline. sh baseline_write is called from baseline_mark_landed, from baseline_after_landing (run_landing's committed/nothing/refused) and from preflight_landing. Grepping '#moe-baseline v1' finds no other header writer.
- The recovery gate (Invoke-MoeRecoveryCheck / preflight_landing step 3) skips on landed=1 BEFORE it probes the marker. That is why a sibling's flag strands A.
- $moeSid / MOE_SID is reset per loop iteration. The pre-flight and the post-flight landing of one iteration share it, and the Moe-Session trailer uses it. Idle recoveries mint a fresh one.
- A pre-flight leaves a LIVE peer's marker alone (Test-MoeLiveMarkerForeignLive / live_marker_foreign_live). In the QA-reject-then-rework trigger the rework session therefore holds NO marker, and QA's exit removes its own.
- Header readers match substrings and regexes (` landed=1`, `head=`, `at=`), so appending ` session=` stays compatible with older twins.
- The ps1 fake proxy answers resume AND blocked claims with task-resume. The sh fake answers them with task-resume and task-blocked. Both fakes tier IN_PROGRESS step affectedFiles as PLANNED.
- All four files are LF. The two .ps1 files carry a UTF-8 BOM.
planningNotes.risks:
1. Marker gap (pre-existing, out of scope). A session that pre-flighted under a live peer's marker holds no marker once that peer exits. Once landed stays 0, a THIRD seat pre-flighting in that window recovers the live bytes as a `recovered` checkpoint: misattribution, no loss, which is the rail's preferred direction. The daemon's finalizing hold (task-758423de) covers the REVIEW handoff. The remaining windows need a live seat's row to be released: a restart give-up after reconcileWindowMs, a manual release_task, or a duplicate seat.
